description:
Publish files as a live website, served over HTTPS at its own URL. Use it when the user asks to publish, host, or share a report, page, dashboard, or other static files at a URL, or names Valet for it. Honor an artifact form the user requests; otherwise choose the form and treatment from its audience, job, and material. A request for a live URL chooses delivery, not one long scrolling page.

The organization's release policies check each publish on Valet's side; a publish that does not meet one is refused or returns an evaluation, and the answer names what to fix.

title and description are required on every publish of files, and a call missing either is refused. Write them for the person who comes back to this page in a month: the site's name is only part of its URL.

files carries text only (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Markdown, JSON, SVG) and suits a few small pages. For a large site or binary assets, call create_push, push with git, and pass push: {id, commit} instead; push needs a site that exists and an account. Pass files or push, not both.

Publishing changes a permanent, private site that already exists: create it first with create_service (kind: site), then publish to its name.

Returns the site's URL and either version or evaluation. In an organization with release policies, an account publish answers with evaluation and no version: the release waits for its policies, and get_evaluation with wait_seconds 20 follows it.

description.description: With files, a call without it is refused. One sentence saying what the site holds, for a person deciding whether to open it. It is shown beside the title wherever the site is listed.

files.description: The site's files. Give this or push, not both. One file named index.html is the minimum; add more for stylesheets, scripts, or further pages.

path.description: Path relative to the site root, with '/' separators and no leading slash: index.html, styles/main.css. It may not contain '.' or '..' segments.

idempotency_key.description: An opaque key of your choosing. Repeating a call with the same key returns the first call's result instead of publishing again, which makes a retry safe.

name.description: The site's name, which is the first label of its URL, https://<name>.<org>.valet.run. The site must exist: create it first with create_service. Publishing to it replaces its files.

org_name.description: The Valet organization to publish into. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

push.description: Publish a Git push instead of files: the id create_push returned and the commit you pushed to its branch. Use it when you can run git with network access, because it sends only what changed. Pass files or push, not both; every other argument keeps its meaning.

commit.description: The full sha of the commit you pushed to the push's branch. The recipe create_push returned prints it.

title.description: With files, a call without it is refused. What the site is called, written for a person: 'Q3 Migration Audit', not a hostname. It labels the site wherever it is listed, so write the same thing the page's own <title> says.

name: publish_site

access.description: Who can open the site: public, private, or password. Change it with set_service_access.

evaluation.description: The release evaluation. Without version, the release waits for its policies: follow it with get_evaluation. With version, the release is live and this is its monitor-only evaluation. Absent when the release has none.

deploy.description: What deploy did with the release: 'waiting' for the policies, 'live', or the code of the refusal. Absent when deploy has not decided.

deploy_message.description: The refusal's message when deploy refused the release. Absent otherwise.

id.description: ID of the release evaluation. Pass it to get_evaluation as evaluation_id.

monitor_findings.description: Count of findings monitor policies reported on a live release. They never block it; get_evaluation shows each. Absent when zero.

monitor_running.description: Names of monitor policies still pending or running on a live release. They never block it. Absent when none are.

status.description: Status of the evaluation across its release policies. get_evaluation lists the per-policy results.

name.description: Name of the site. It is the first label of its URL.

no_changes.description: True when the pushed tree is what the site already serves, so nothing was published. Absent otherwise.

org.description: Name of the Valet organization the call acted in.

url.description: URL that serves the site. Absent while the site has no route.

version.description: Version number of the release the publish made live. Absent when no release went live: the release waits for its policies (see evaluation) or nothing changed.

title: Publish a website
